categories.label: Price
categories.purpose: Read the raw traded price and the individual bar’s own open, high, low, and close.
whenToUse: Show the level a decision is being made at.
Reference a bar’s own extremes rather than a derived deviation.
bestPractices: Use the last traded price for the live level and a bar fact for what the bar did.
Read the bar state when a provisional bar would change the interpretation.
commonMisuses: Treating the perpetual mark as the traded price — they are separate metrics.
Comparing raw price levels across assets instead of a percentage relation.

examples.title: Last traded price
examples.description: Read the live traded price, independent of any candle rung.

categories.label: Momentum
categories.purpose: Describe directional impulse, exhaustion, and the pace of price movement.
whenToUse: Confirm whether a move has participation.
Identify overextended or diverging momentum.
bestPractices: Pair level readings with trajectories.
Interpret oscillator extremes in market context.
commonMisuses: Treating an overbought reading as an automatic short.
Stacking several correlated oscillators as independent evidence.

examples.title: RSI trajectory
examples.description: Track the recent RSI build-up and direction.

categories.label: Trend
categories.purpose: Describe direction, persistence, and price location relative to trend references.
whenToUse: Confirm directional structure.
Measure price extension from a moving reference.
bestPractices: Use slower references for regime context and faster references for timing.
Read distance together with direction.
commonMisuses: Assuming a lagging average predicts a reversal.
Comparing trend levels without matching timeframes.

examples.title: Distance from SMA 20
examples.description: Measure signed price extension from the 20-period simple moving average.

categories.label: Volatility
categories.purpose: Describe the magnitude and expansion or contraction of market movement.
whenToUse: Calibrate risk to current movement.
Identify squeeze or expansion conditions.
bestPractices: Separate movement size from direction.
Compare volatility on the same timeframe as the decision.
commonMisuses: Reading high volatility as inherently bullish or bearish.
Using raw price-unit volatility across unlike assets.

examples.title: Current ATR
examples.description: Read the latest average true range on the strategy timeframe.

categories.label: Volume & Flow
categories.purpose: Describe participation and the balance of buying and selling pressure.
whenToUse: Confirm whether price movement has participation.
Spot flow divergence from price.
Set an absolute activity floor, which needs the raw quantity rather than a ratio.
bestPractices: Use ratios when comparing activity across assets.
Treat flow as confirmation rather than a standalone direction.
Use the raw quantity for a single-coin read or a threshold, and the ratio for a cohort column.
commonMisuses: Equating high volume with bullish demand.
Comparing raw volume counts across structurally different markets.
Comparing raw base-unit volume across assets — that compares denominations, not activity (44,723 BTC beside 2,100,000 DOGE); use the ratio for cohort columns.
Reading a raw per-bar quantity off the forming bar, whose volume ramps from zero each interval — a closed-bar trajectory is the honest read.

examples.title: Volume participation
examples.description: Read current volume relative to its baseline.

categories.label: Derivatives
categories.purpose: Describe positioning, leverage demand, and funding pressure in perpetual markets.
whenToUse: Assess crowded positioning.
Confirm whether exposure is entering or leaving the market.
bestPractices: Combine funding with open-interest change.
Use windowed context for noisy periodic rates.
commonMisuses: Treating positive funding as an immediate short signal.
Interpreting open-interest growth without price context.

examples.title: Funding mean
examples.description: Average the canonical funding history window.

categories.label: Structure
categories.purpose: Describe price location, reference levels, and active support or resistance zones.
whenToUse: Plan entries around meaningful levels.
Measure room to nearby support or resistance.
bestPractices: Select the side relevant to the proposed direction.
Use structure with momentum or flow confirmation.
commonMisuses: Treating every nearby level as equally strong.
Applying a separate timeframe override to anchor-derived zones.

examples.title: Nearest support distance
examples.description: Measure signed distance to the nearest active support zone.

categories.label: Regime
categories.purpose: Describe the platform-classified trend, volatility, and momentum environment.
whenToUse: Adapt tactics to the current market state.
Check whether conditions are changing across observations.
bestPractices: Use regime as context for other evidence.
Review trajectories when transition risk matters.
commonMisuses: Treating a regime label as a guaranteed trade direction.
Reconstructing regime labels from unrelated client heuristics.

examples.title: Trend-regime trajectory
examples.description: Show the recent canonical trend-regime sequence.

categories.label: Crowd
categories.purpose: Describe aggregate player positioning, confidence, and historical accuracy.
whenToUse: Compare market evidence with participant consensus.
Identify crowded or contrarian conditions.
bestPractices: Treat crowd measures as contextual evidence.
Distinguish popularity from demonstrated accuracy.
commonMisuses: Assuming consensus is always correct.
Using crowd values as candle-timeframe indicators.

examples.title: Crowd pick rate
examples.description: Read the current platform-wide pick rate.

categories.label: Derived
categories.purpose: Describe platform-owned cross-family classifications and convergence facts.
whenToUse: Summarize agreement across canonical evidence families.
Expose platform truth-table outcomes directly.
bestPractices: Use the derived label as a summary and retain its underlying context.
Read the declared vocabulary exactly.
commonMisuses: Recomputing the classification with client-local rules.
Treating a summary label as proof that every input agrees.

examples.description: Read the canonical price-and-flow alignment classification.
